newsitem.title: USA: Calif. authorities arrest six, seize explosives.
newsitem.headline: Calif. authorities arrest six, seize explosives.

text.p: California authorities have arrested six men, some suspected of links to anti-government groups, and seized explosives powerful enough to "have leveled three city blocks," officials said on Thursday.

Law enforcement officers seized 500 pounds (225 kgs) of petrogel explosive at a home in Yuba City, 50 miles (80 kms) north of Sacramento, on Wednesday, Yuba County Undersheriff Gary Finch told Reuters.
Finch said that had they had gone off, the explosives "could have leveled three city blocks." Officials believe the explosives were obtained illegally from a mining company in Montana, he said.
"What they planned to do with it (the explosives) we don't know," Finch said.
Authorities went to the house looking for someone connected with William Goehler, who was injured in an explosion that badly damaged his home in nearby Olivehurst last Sunday.

Goehler, 34, a sympathiser with the anti-government Freemen group which was involved in an 81-day standoff with the FBI in Montana last year, was arrested and charged with possessing explosives after his release from the hospital on Monday, Finch said.
Kevin Quinn, 37, and Vernon Weckner, 66, who lived at the home where the large quantity of explosives was found, were arrested and charged with having explosives, Finch said.

The authorities believed some explosives might be missing from the cases and information from one of the suspects helped them find another 5 pounds (2.25 kgs) of explosives at another location early on Thursday morning, Finch said.
Jason Fox, 19, Edward Whitlow, 22, and Robert Deaver, 33, were also arrested and charged with possessing explosives, bringing to six the total in custody, Finch said.
Deaver was also charged with child endangerment because he had two children, aged 4 and 5, in the house where the 5 pounds of explosives were found, Finch said.

Authorities believe some of the men in custody are linked to anti-government militia groups, he said without giving details. Finch said all the men were connected with one another but he did not know if they were all belonged to the same group.
The chain of events was set in motion by Sunday's explosion in Olivehurst. The blast, which could be heard for miles, caused extensive damage to Goehler's house and broke windows in nearby buildings.
Goehler suffered a neck injury while his wife Debbie and one of his children were slightly injured. Authorities believe explosives stored in a tree near the house blew up.
News reports said Goehler went to Montana during last year's Freemen standoff, spending weeks near the militants' compound carrying an upside-down American flag.

The heavily armed Freemen, who rejected U.S. government authority, set up what they saw as an independent state on a Montana ranch, calling it "Justus Township." They eventually surrendered to authorities.
